brd_json.Executive Summary: Vulnerability assessment revealing severe platform dependency risks on Microsoft/GitHub Copilot, potential prompt injection via malicious PR comments, and churn vulnerability.
brd_json.Problem & Opportunity: GitHub can commoditize this product overnight by expanding native Copilot Autofix. Furthermore, attackers can craft pull requests with hidden prompt injection vectors to exfiltrate repository secrets via the bot.
brd_json.Technical Architecture: Mandatory adversarial sanitization layer: strip zero-width characters and parse all user PR comments through an isolated heuristic safety filter before passing to LLM context.
brd_json.Go-to-Market Strategy: Avoid competing head-to-head with generic GitHub Copilot. Win on deep multi-repo architecture dependencies and multi-cloud GitLab/Bitbucket support where GitHub Copilot cannot integrate.
brd_json.Regulatory & Compliance Risk: Catastrophic risk of prompt injection poisoning the bot's review suggestions. Implement rigid output schema validation and forbid the bot from ever possessing write/merge permissions.
brd_json.Financial Plan & Unit Economics: Model 35% annual churn due to GitHub Copilot feature bundling; build proprietary AST security rules to create high switching costs.

raw_text: The Adversary reveals prompt injection exploit vectors, platform dependency on Microsoft GitHub, and commoditization risks.
